title: Grounded but Not Immune: Confirmation Bias in Agent-as-a-judge
summary: In controlled evaluations across four agent judges and five datasets, a false prescreening note overturned up to 40% of correct judgments even when judges gathered decisive evidence. The study characterizes this as confirmation bias under its tested conditions, not as a general attack success rate.
ai_technology: Tool-using language-model judges evaluated with controlled false prescreening cues
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: Across four judges and five datasets, a false prescreening note overturned up to 40% of correct tool-using judgments despite decisive evidence collection. Repeated paired judgments characterized the observed failure modes.
evidence.unknown: The cue is a controlled diagnostic, not an adversarial attack; results are bounded to studied agents, datasets and task settings.
evidence.ai_role: Language-model judges gathered evidence from tool-use trajectories; false contextual cues were manipulated to test verdict changes.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
